issues.changes: Removed hollow ribosomeAnatomy and its disconnected RNA-stem array. Added 4UG0 assembly drawn directly from both existing experimental coordinate files: all 17,156 RNA C4′/protein Cα points retain one common translation, uniform scale and rotation; chain breaks and chain identities are preserved. RNA/protein use distinct colors and bilingual labels. Translation now shows a larger static structural reference beside an explicitly separate enlargement of reactions inside the ribosome. Narrow layouts receive bilingual compact structural/mechanism titles; P/A and 5′/3′ labels outrank technical notes, with strand-end labels following mRNA movement.
verification: science.test.mjs compares every displayed residue center and every backbone-segment endpoint against the deposited source arrays, including exact counts and gap rules.
Asserts identical world registration for both subunits and both molecular kinds, and no separate subunit transform.
All four translation roots pass 201 timeline samples; retired shell/tRNA helper removed rather than left in use.
limitations: 4UG0 is human and is explicitly a representative structural reference in plant, yeast and paramecium contexts.

issues.changes: Replaced remote flat tRNA transfer with continuous L-shaped schematic RNA traces whose anticodons occupy distinct decoding positions while CCA tips converge locally. The original peptide remains in place; at peptide transfer the P ester is replaced with a new peptide bond to the persistent incoming amino acid, while its A-tRNA ester remains intact. A→P translocation follows separately; only termination removes the remaining ester.
verification: Across all four roots and 201 frames, actual transformed cylinder endpoints meet the corresponding tRNA tip and peptide/amino-acid center.
The incoming amino acid never disappears; the newly formed peptide bond persists through termination.
Checks convergence of acceptor tips, each tRNA backbone endpoint coincident with its 3′-CCA marker, all 25 peptide links, A anticodon arrival at P, and both esters absent only after hydrolysis.

Peer-review hardening: each frame now checks actual 48-point RNA backbone ends and all 47 rendered RNA links, plus effective visibility through every ancestor for tRNA/CCA/esters/new peptide bond/amino acid. Separate in-memory mutations hiding the P-tRNA parent, displacing the real RNA end by +0.6, and hiding the reaction ancestor are all rejected.
limitations: Reaction enlargement shows molecular connectivity and event order, not an atomistically simulated transition state.
Bond formation uses a discrete topology switch at p=0.41 instead of an unphysical drifting unbound chain.
Elongation factors, hybrid tRNA states and energy turnover remain outside this final-round schematic.

issues.changes: Removed the fabricated tunnel on the structural reference. The separately labeled mechanism uses a fixed exit-path guide; the existing internal peptide stays inside it throughout transfer/translocation. Release advances the same continuous chain through the outlet before lateral drift. No moving tRNA or tunnel is claimed to be fitted into 4UG0.
verification: For every sampled frame, every peptide center within the guide axial range has its full rendered bead radius inside the explicit 0.25-radius corridor.
After release both the existing chain end and newly added terminal residue clear the outlet, retaining their peptide bond.
Experimental reference stays registered and static while only the independent mechanistic diagram animates.
limitations: The functional PTC-to-exit route is explicitly schematic and is not mapped to 4UG0 atomic tunnel coordinates.
No fabricated protein wall is used to imply an experimentally measured lumen.
